title: Spanish SailGP team bought by Israeli billionaire Idan Ofer’s Quantum Pacific Group
content:
Editor’s note: This story is part of The Athletic’s coverage of SailGP, an international sailing competition that has been likened to Formula 1 on water. Follow SailGP here.

Quantum Pacific Group, the conglomerate owned by Israeli billionaire Idan Ofer, has bought Los Gallos, the Spanish-based team in the global sailing competition SailGP.

Co-founded by three-time America’s Cup winner Sir Russell Coutts and Oracle Corporation boss Larry Ellison in 2018, the high-speed, close-to-shore racing format has attracted investment from a stellar cast of business tycoons, celebrities and sports stars.

Ofer, who also owns stakes in LaLiga’s Atletico Madrid, Portuguese football club Famalicao and Spanish cycling team Movistar, joins the likes of Hollywood trio Anne Hathaway, Hugh Jackman and Ryan Reynolds, Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe and heavyweight boxer Deontay Wilder as an owner of a SailGP team.

The son of Israeli shipping magnate Sammy Ofer, Idan Ofer now has interests in energy, mining, shipping and sports, and has amassed a fortune of more than $30billion (£22billion).

Led by Olympic gold medallist Diego Botin, Los Gallos won the fourth edition of SailGP in 2024 and are fifth in the 2026 standings after three of 13 events.

How much Quantum Pacific paid for Los Gallos, who were previously owned by SailGP, has not been revealed but it is likely to be in the region of the $60million (£45million) Orlando Magic owner Doug DeVos shelled out on Danish-based outfit Rockwool Racing SailGP Team in February.

“The Spanish team is a natural fit,” said Quantum Pacific chief executive Antoine Bonnier in a press release to announce the deal.

“The Iberian region is a market we know well and believe in fully. And SailGP, with its global audience and elite competitive format, is exactly the kind of high-growth sport platform we believe in. We are here to win and build something that lasts.”

If this move is half as profitable as Ofer’s investment in Atletico, Quantum Pacific will certainly be able to claim a big win. He bought 15 percent of Atletico for €50m in 2017, when the Spanish side was worth about €330m. He doubled that stake at the same valuation a year later but then sold 3 percent of the club to American sports fund Apollo last month for €75m, leaving him with a 25 per ent stake in a business now worth €2.5bn.

Los Gallos’ purchase means that 12 of the 13 teams have now been sold by SailGP, which topped $200m in annual revenue last year.

“This is another hugely significant milestone for SailGP and for the continued growth of the championship,” said SailGP managing director Andrew Thompson.

“Quantum Pacific brings a deep understanding of sport performance, commercial success and the maritime world. Spain is a cornerstone market for us, defined by its rich sporting culture, incredibly passionate fanbase and a winning SailGP team.”

The next race in the 2026 Rolex SailGP Championship is in Rio de Janeiro on April 11-12.
